newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 30.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
INDIA, CHINA TAKE SUBSTANTIAL PEACE INITIATIVES

India and China took substantial peace initiatives by pledging not to use their military capability against each other. They also agreed to a series of confidence building measures (CBMs), including negotiated force reductions in mutually defined geographical zones along the Line of Actual Control. An agreement to this effect was signed between India's Foreign Minister I K Gujral and Chinese counterpart Qian Qichen following talks between the Indian leaders and the visiting Chinese delegation led by President Jiang Zemin. The CBMs provide for several measures, including avoidance of military exercise involving more than a division (nearly 1,500 troops) ear the line of control.
The Economic Times
NEW COAL POLICY ON ANVIL

The K.S. Chari committee on coal has recommended the setting up of an independent agency at national level to step up exploration of coal and lignite resources as well as deregulation of coal prices in a phased manner and competitive bidding for new coal and lignite blocks. The Chari committee has been set up to formulate an integrated coal policy for the Ninth and Tenth Plan periods (1997-2007 AD). Its recommendations are being considered by the coal ministry. The committee has representations from the ministries of power, coal, steel and railways. This was stated in the Parliament by Union minister of state for coal Kanti Singh.
IMPORT OF GOLD UNDER SIL MAY BE INCREASED

The government might consider increasing the entitlement of gold imports under special import licence, Commerce Secretary Tejendra Khanna said. A reduction in the duty on gold, currently pegged at five percent ad valorem, and storage of gold in bonded warehouses might also be allowed. Khanna said these changes might be incorporated in the forthcoming Export Import Policy, slated for March 1997. However, there was no question of placing gold imports under open general licence in the short or medium term, the commerce secretary added.
224 MLN RUPEE LOSS SENDS SIEMENS SCRIP CRASHING

Siemens Ltd scrip slumped to a 52-week low of 423 rupees on the Bombay bourse after the company declared a 239 million rupee net loss for the six months period ending to September 31, 1996 (224 million rupees). Losses were attributed to the company's telecommunication business. The substantial increase in interest cost (481 million rupees against 204.5 million rupees a year ago), coupled with higher depreciation too adversely affected the company's bottomline. The net loss came despite a 24 percent increase in Siemen's turnover during the six months at 6.63 billion rupees (5.33 billion rupees). PLANNERS, FINANCE MINISTRY DEADLOCKED OVER PLAN SIZE

The differences between the Planning Commission and the finance ministry over the size of the Ninth Plan created a deadlock at the meeting of the full Planning Commission. The commission discussed the draft plan but failed to reach any agreement on the most crucial issue of size of the Ninth Plan. Finance Minister P. Chidambaram did some plain speaking at the meeting about the planners' demand and the overall resource position. Despite Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's attempt to persuade the finance minister, the latter argued it was not possible to give a budgetary support of more than 3000 billion rupees, as against the planners proposal of 3750 billion rupees, for the Ninth Plan.
SAMSUNG TO RECEIVE ONLY FIVE PCT ROYALTY

The government has cleared the joint venture (JV) between Samsung Electronics Corporation and Larsen & Toubro (L&T) for the manufacture of telecommunications equipment. But it has reduced the annual royalty to be paid to the Korean company five percent. Samsung had asked for a seven percent royalty on the total annual sales of the JV. The initial investment in the JV will be $4 million which will rise to a total of $44 million. The equity component is slated to be $2 million with Samsung holding 51 percent equity and L&T the rest. The JV will start operations in 1997, with EPABXs, which will be followed by network equipment for paging using advanced digital signal processing technology.
FIIs LOWER PURCHASE OF STOCKS IN NOVEMBER

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) slowed down their purchases of Indian stocks significantly in November. Securities and Exchange Board of India figures showed the net monthly investments made by FIIs to November 22 stood at $86 million, compared to $233 million in October. Cumulative FII investment in the country stood at $7.11 billion, while total inflows since January 1996 stood closer to $3 billion.
Business Standard
CORPORATES MAKE BEELINE FOR ADRS

Undeterred by the experience of BPL Cellular Holdings, half a dozen companies have approached the government for permission to access the American Depository Receipt markets. BPL Cellular has made the country's first direct equity offerings to U.S. investors. Finance ministry sources indicated pending applications comprised both private and public firms, including Bharti Telecom and Max Hutchison. The public telecommunication major Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd is also hoping to capitalise on this trend.
TOTAL AUTONOMY FOR BOURSE REGULATOR MOOTED

The bourse regulator (SEBI) economists' forum in its last meeting unanimously called for giving complete autonomy to the SEBI. The panel also called for widening the investor base by allowing pension funds and provident funds to invest freely in the securities markets.
THAPARS OPT OUT OF NYLON VENTURE WITH DUPONT

The Thapars decided to opt out of Thapar-DuPont Ltd, the joint venture set up to implement a $200 million nylon 6,6 project in the country. As part of a deal finalised recently, DuPont would buy out the 50 percent stake of the Thapars in the company at an undisclosed price. Sources said the U.S. company was also talking to Mitsui, holding five percent in the company, to buy out the Japanese conglomerate's stake, too. DuPont would soon apply to the Foreign Investment Promotion Board for permission to hike its stake in Thapar-DuPont from the existing 45 percent to 100 percent, converting the venture into a fully owned subsidiary, sources added.
HLL BOARD RECAST PLANNED AFTER MERGER WITH BBLIL

Major top level changes and a restructuring of the post-merger Hindustan Lever Ltd (HLL) board will mark the formal merger of Brooke Bond Lipton India Ltd (BBLIL) with HLL. The merger is pending with the Calcutta High Court. The new-look HLL board will comprise the chairman, the executive vice-chairman, 11 full-time directors, and two to three external directors. The new board of directors will have three members from BBLIL. Significant among the changes is the fact that several board members of BBLIL have been posted abroad to pave the way for the new management structure at the country's largest consumer product company. Some others in BBLIL are due for retirement.
Business Line
MUTUAL FUNDS TOLD TO FOLLOW CENTRAL BANK GUIDELINES

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) said the money market mutual fund (MMMF) investments would be in accordance with the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) investment guidelines. Sources said the mutual fund industry had been waiting for the SEBI decision in this regard since November 23, 1995, when RBI revised the investment guidelines for MMMFs. SEBI officials said while the structure of MMMFs would be similar to that of existing mutual funds, the investments of such funds (or schemes launched by existing mutual funds) would be in accordance with the RBI guidelines.
